articles.detail: 5 cycles completed; metrics window counts 26 (cycle logs avg ~9/cycle, avgPublished 9)

experiment: Skipped. No active experiments to evaluate; no pause gate. The lone metric miss (tech 2 vs 4) is single-day variance, not a systemic regression, and the tech floor is already at its range max for the selector lever.
weakestArea: Tech, at 2 articles (~8% of output), is furthest from target (4/day). But this is day-to-day variance on a low-volume day (26 articles vs 56 yesterday, when tech was 9), not a trend. The tech category floor is already at 3/cycle; raising it to 4 (range max) off one anomalous day isn't justified, and the 2026-05-09 sourcing experiment established that selector floors are a largely tapped lever. Sci+tech ratio still cleared 25% (35%) because science carried 7, so educational coverage held even with tech soft.
watching: Tech volume: 2 today vs 9 yesterday — confirm it recovers next cycle before treating as a pattern.
Total output dropped to 26 from 56 — likely a light news day, but worth confirming the feed/selector didn't under-fill.
Multi-source sat exactly at the floor of 4; one fewer would breach. Feed multi-source supply (~9/cycle) remains the binding cap per 2026-05-09 learning.
Freshness data is thin (count=2 valid lags today) — median 0 is reliable directionally but based on few datapoints.
coverageGaps: No Africa (AF) or Oceania (OC) representation today; concentration in AM/EU/ME.
Tech sourcing narrow — only Nature and Dawn tagged as tech sources, no dedicated tech specialist outlets (Ars Technica, MIT Tech Review, The Diplomat) surfaced today.
context: Clean operational day: 5/5 cycles completed, 0 duplicates, top-source share healthy at 15%, freshness at 0. The history shows the selector category-floor lever has been worked hard (tech 2->3 kept Apr, multi-source floors raised then reverted May) and is near exhaustion for sourcing/diversity gains — future improvements there should target the upstream feed (Event Registry clustering, regional outlet inclusion) rather than selector floors. The queued numerical-density experiment touches write-prompt.md (out of daily-tuning scope) and remains a writer-stage item for the weekly reflect.
